column1: # DEV-b: project environments and secrets (envs) and the mise tools. Format: see the header of ~/.config/hub/hub.

column9: Projects -> environments -> variables of the Bitwarden folder Env/<project>, one Secure Note per environment, one hidden field per secret. Values are masked everywhere; Enter/y copies one (cleared after 30 s), v shows it for 15 s, e edits, a adds, u selects the environment of a project (prod asks for its name and expires after an hour), c copies values to another environment, i imports a .env file, x writes .env.example. Secrets reach only the command: `envs run -- CMD` (or `er CMD`), never the shell. Opened from the hub it starts at the project list; inside a project directory (tmux prefix v) it starts at that project.

column3: Use an environment (dev, stage, prod) in this project
column9: Selects the active environment of the project in the current directory; prod needs its name typed and expires after an hour. The prompt shows [stage] or a red [prod] while a non-default environment is selected. Run it from the project directory (tmux prefix v shows the same list).

column3: Import a .env file into Bitwarden and mise
column9: Reads .env in the project directory, asks which variables are secrets (Bitwarden, hidden fields) and which are plain (mise [env], committed), then offers to shred the file; a file tracked by git is kept with a warning to rotate the values.

column3: Check the bound projects (names, binding, vault)
column9: Per bound project: .envs.toml validity, binding, conflicts with mise [env], plain .env files, a tracked .env (error), mise trust and tools, and with an unlocked vault the items, missing and undeclared fields. No values are read out.

column3: mise: tool versions of this directory
column9: Lists the tools mise sees from the current directory and where each version is pinned (.mise.toml, .nvmrc, ...). Projects pin versions in .mise.toml; outside a project the system go, node and python are used.
